articles.description: — Rueben Chinyelu posted his first double-double of the season and made the first 3-pointer of his college career as No. 3 Florida escaped with a 76-67 victory against Milwaukee on Tuesday night.

articles.headline: Colorado rallies from 20-point deficit, beats Stanford 70-65 at Acrisure Series
articles.description: — Barrington Hargress had 19 points on 7-of-8 shooting, Justin Neely scored 16 and Colorado overcame a 20-point deficit and beat Stanford 70-65 on Tuesday night at the Acrisure Series.

articles.headline: Louisville's Kelsey tells 5th-year critics 'bring it' as Trimble shines in upset
articles.description: After Seth Trimble led Louisville to a 72-64 win over No. 5 Texas Tech, Cardinals coach Pat Kelsey told critics of teams using fifth-year players, "Everybody can have their opinion. Bring it."

images.name: Seth Trimble [600x400]
images.caption: Seth Trimble scored 24 points in Tuesday's win over No. 5 Texas Tech that gave Louisville its first victory over an AP top-five opponent under coach Pat Kelsey.

article.story: PHILADELPHIA -- — Tyler Perkins had 23 points and Jake Fiegan hit four 3-pointers and scored 15 to help Villanova close out a much-needed 79-73 win over No. 18 Michigan on Saturday night. Elijah Crawford added 13 points for the Wildcats (4-2) and Luigi Suigo, the 7-foot-3 freshman dubbed the Italian Wemby, had nine points and six rebounds. Trey McKenney scored 22 for Michigan (3-2). Elliot Cadeau, the Most Outstanding Player at the Final Four last season, missed all six of his first-half shots but finished with 11 points. Villanova topped Michigan in the 2018 national championship game and the banner to celebrate that title was raised in the arena rafters. The Wildcats are far removed from those glory years and missed three straight NCAA Tournaments before coach Kevin Willard got them back in the bracket last season. The early returns on a path to a second consecutive tournament appearance yielded frustrating results on the Main Line. Villanova held a one-point lead with about 12 minutes left Tuesday at Pittsburgh before it collapsed and was outscored 31-10 down the stretch in a 20-point loss. The Wildcats also blew a 10-point lead to Notre Dame in the season opener in Italy, tough giveaways in the nonconference portion of the schedule — especially with a game Friday at No. 11 Kansas on the horizon. They almost blew it again against the defending NCAA champions. The Wildcats missed 11 straight shots, helping Michigan whittle a 17-point deficit down to six. Crawford hit a tough fadeaway in the paint to finally make one and the Wildcats — who saw their lead shrink to 77-73 — held on from the free-throw line. Fiegan provided a boost early in the second half when he buried consecutive 3s that stretched Villanova's lead to 58-45. Devin Royal hit one from the corner that finally got a rise out of the half-full crowd. Perkins, a rarity on the roster as a third-season standout, cut for a driving layup that made it 63-46 and gave the Wildcats the cushion they needed over the final tenuous minutes. The Wolverines have had trouble this season in national championship rematches. Their other loss this month was to UConn in a rematch of the 2026 NCAA title game. Up next Michigan plays Tuesday at Creighton. Villanova hosts Coppin State on Tuesday. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here.
